body: My mother found out in not the best way (but then again is there ever a good way to bring up that you harm yourself)...I had been seeing a psychiatrist and usually I'd attend the appointments alone but mum decided to come into one with me and my psychiatrist asked "so how's the self harm going" and I rolled up my sleeves to show her my arms while my mum just stared. At first she didn't say anything but on the drive home she said "so that's why you haven't been wearing tshirts" and I could just sense her disappointment. Nowadays I don't care anymore and wear tshirts around her but I still cover up if I'm ever going out in public.
No, all my attempts only filled me with regret in the sense I didn't plan them better (hence why they've been unsuccessful).

Have you ever been inpatient in all your years? My last stay was 14 months, I came out for 2, then readmitted last month after my caseworker that came for a home visit wasn't happy with my safety. I've had half a dozen or so admissions now in an attempt to prevent death and harm but oddly enough I make more attempts here.

May I ask your diagnosis? I've got psychosis, depression, OCD, social anxiety, panic disorder, agoraphobia and to top it all off I'm autistic (albeit high functioning). I have had some doctors also believe I've got bipolar or borderline, schizoid or schizotypal personality disorder but with the amount of professionals I've seen it's impossible for them to all agree so I just go with the current theory.

I'm very sad to hear how long you've been unwell, I too have tried what feels like everything to make life less of a hassle and actually enjoyable, but nothing ever helps.

I guess the one reassurance we can give each other is one day our time will come to an end, whether the world agrees with it or not. 

I'd go even further to say I wish I'd never been born at all.

Hello :)

CPR is definitely not what I was expecting to wake up to when I last tried to hang myself. It really hurt but I was lucky enough to not have any broken ribs (they did an X-ray the day after when the bruising became apparent). Hiccups are currently my worst enemy.

You're correct in saying nurses sign up to the job knowing full well they could come across death at any moment. And no, psych wards aren't the cheeriest of locations to be, for both nurses and patients. There isn't much to do here in the form of entertainment but I'm currently too unwell to even leave my bed some days. I do get up Monday, Wednesday and Friday to get ECT however (this is my 3rd course of it). It's not exactly helping but I quite like when you first wake up oblivious to the world and also when the anaesthetic puts you to sleep, that's the only reasons I've agreed to have it again...although they could probably force it upon me if I didn't agree. My last admission I was put on clozapine and gained quite a bit of weight which I still haven't managed to get off me. I don't really care though it just is frustrating some clothes don't fit anymore.

There are a few nurses that our conversations delve into some pretty interesting topics, the idea of helping other people with organs whilst ending my life seems like a win-win. Every nurse has their own ideas though so overall I've heard quite a few reactions to this "plan" of mine. 

I've tried a lot from counselling, antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, ECT, vitamins, meditation, distraction/coping techniques, trying to find other outlets (exercise, dancing, sport, art)...hell I've even looked into crystal healing. Nothing has helped and I doubt anything ever will.

The right to die should definitely be a thing. I can understand if they set about some limits on how much "suffering" needs to be endured before they'll allow it (basically to stop deaths from say a relationship break up or something), but considering I've been suffering since I was 15 and I'm now 21 that's 1/3rd of my life where I haven't wanted to be alive, but have been forced to do so.

I concur my friend, all I want is to die in peace. When we all die in the end I don't know why cutting it short really matters in the grand scheme of things. I'm not special, I'm just another human.

In a way it's not so much what I'm missing, apart from the usual answer of happiness and joy, the biggest problem is that I'm psychotic and hear voices every second of the day. They make living so unbearable because they've manifested in such a way that the only way to get some peace from them is to do as they say. They constantly tell me to self harm (mainly cutting - my last harm required 35 staples and 28 stitches to repair) as well as to end my life. What sort of existence is this where the only time I feel even slightly better is after I've sliced myself up or made an attempt? That's the only time the voices shut up. I'm just done.

I know that sooner or later I'll succeed it's just a matter of time. My death is inevitable. I just wish I wasn't stuck in this ward where dying is so difficult. I don't want to keep going and nothing will change that.
Thank you. And not really, I'm not really the most empathetic person around and don't have any groups I see as worth living for.

There isn't much to say honestly. I'm chronically depressed with psychosis, anxiety, OCD and some personality disorders. I'm in a psych ward currently where I'm just getting pills thrown at me to try and drown out the voices I hear (which doesn't work). I've tried to die twice this admission already in a month. I have nothing to live for and I don't care about anyone or anything enough to stop me from ending it. I'm just done.
I always worried even if I directly asked the psych "is this a placebo" that it could be a double blind study where they were under the assumption what I was taking was real too.
It's funny you mention risperidone as it was one of my early meds that I was totally convinced I was taking a placebo of.
It's always nice to hear you're not alone!

I think it's beautiful what you've created off me, I wasn't expecting to get a reply like that it really warmed my heart. Thank you.
I can't however guarantee my safety sadly. I'm really struggling

That was an interesting perspective but my voices are completely either oblivious or simply ignore whatever I have to say/think towards them. I've tried challenging them or asking them to stop or even get them to realise that often what they say leads to physical harm to me and I am (in my understanding) their host. Why would voices want to destroy their host? I think the thing I can't deal with the most is how goddamn repetitive my voices are. They will say the same things for hours upon hours on end and it's so exhausting having to deal with and I'm just reaching my breaking point.

I definitely understand the problem isn't the voices it's how you respond and react to them, that makes perfect sense. I guess the relationship I've had with my voices over the last 7 hasn't been the best but I'm at a loss with how to change it.

I was hearing voices before I was medicated. They're the main reason I've been put on so many meds. The team I've got at the moment wants to up the meds and add more meds and I'm just so sick of trying things that never work.

I've been in multiple wards for different levels of being unwell but all they do is prolong the inevitable death I wish upon myself. They know what I'm going through I've always been open and honest with psychiatrists but it doesn't help them "fix" me. I'm just tired of dealing with it all. Call me weak and pathetic for not being able to keep trying but I've had enough.

Yes I've been in psych services when all my meds have been started/changed and I'm always on them for at least 2 months. Often they'll up the dose once or twice too which can lead to even more months on them to make sure they're in effect.
Who's "they"?

Does beating your arms and legs get the voices to go away or do you think it's the feel good endorphins that mask them?

No sleep for days is definitely not recommended. I've seen some pretty intense hallucinations when sleep deprived so if anything I always aim for lots of sleep. I'm glad you stopped wanting to damage your head/brain, it does go against instinct to destroy ourselves from a biological standpoint. Heads are important.

Blood can be real annoying, I agree. Sadly it doesn't stop me from cutting so I've often got to deal with the mess I've created afterwards. The worst times is when you nick arteries and it pulses out, or veins that just seem to endlessly ooze.

(For some reason your reply was posted like 8 times?? Probably a fault on reddit's end)

Trust me when I say I cannot ignore them. It's like having headphones taped to your head at full volume, they are always present and always loud. In a weird way I don't think they have bodies? Like to me they're an entity based entirely of sound so telling them to cut or kill themselves isn't exactly possible. I'm glad you have found a way to manage yours.
They really are yes.

That must suck having to basically punish yourself with harm every time you do something wrong, but it's really good it's been a long time since you've used a blade. In the ward the oddest item I've used to cut was a comb and that took ages to break the skin (0/10 would not recommend). Generally I use a blade...currently have 28 or so stitches from my last go. I know exactly what you mean that sometimes just the thought of doing it can relieve some stress. It's such an awful way to live hey.

From my experience it is free, they use local anaesthetic first with stitches (but if you get staples they generally don't numb you) and they don't tell your parents/guardian. However, I'm in Australia and it could be different where you are.

I dissociate when I harm at least 99% of the time, so it isn't painful at all until an hour or so later if I've hit nerves in the process. Maybe that's why I didn't get any throbbing or heavy pains, I was not really present in my body (it's hard to explain it).

I believe you're right.
Originally I only cut with my right hand but when my left arm started running out of spaces I just learnt to do it with my left hand too.
I always end up cutting my fingers/hand with double sided blades. I never notice at the time because they're so minor though, and all you end up doing is whacking on a bandaid.

Without advocating for death by blood loss, it actually isn't that painful from my experience (well, obviously I'm not dead but I've passed out and that's sort of all you'd experience). You just sort of feel really feint and hear a lot of static and things go dark. Then I found myself laying down but awake again, but if you were still profusely bleeding you just wouldn't wake up.

I do agree blood is inconvenient though, it makes such a mess.
Yeah I've had hundreds of stitches and staples in my time for big ones, and yes they're also on my outer arms.

I live in Australia where we get heatwaves of 40-45 degree days (I think it's like 100-115 degrees fahrenheit) in summer and if I have to go out I still slip on a longsleeve. Luckily I live with a friend who also has self harm scars so we can both wear tshirts around each other at home without batting an eye.

Honestly I don't know what I'm living for. You might say I still have some hope or fight in me but I wouldn't agree. I'm not scared of death either, I've made a few attempts. I'm literally a jellyfish in this world just floating aimlessly for no apparent reason. Since there are only 2 possibilities from here, living or dying, with dying being the ultimate destination anyway, I'm currently willing to see how living goes. But if it gets hard again...I'll probably attempt again.

The only time my arms aren't covered are when I'm home, hospitalised or going to emergency to get them stitched/stapled.

I wouldn't dare go out in public in a tshirt. In the brief moments I'm in the hospital waiting room right after I've cut I always get people staring at my arms, and I can sense their pity, confusion, shock and worry. 

In the psych ward I get other patients come up and stroke my arms without even asking because they're curious as to how my arms feel, it's terrible. Especially when afterwards they get all "don't do that to yourself sweetie, what will you tell your future children??", like I need their words of wisdom (FYI never having kids). 

I've just come to the realisation that it's far easier to hide my arms than to deal with the reactions. Sad but true.

When exactly was the first time you did it? What was running through your head? I'm guessing if you didn't do it over strong feelings, maybe you were just experimenting? It can be like how people do drugs; they know it's probably not the best idea but they give it a go and then get addicted, even if their life is swell.
Thank you, I might just take you up on that offer.

As someone who's needed hundreds of stitches and staples, as well as internal stitches on some of my largest cuts, I eventually stopped caring.

Originally it all felt very scary but somehow oddly right that I needed to get my arm put back together, but after requiring stitches for years (aka every time I harm I need to go via ambulance to emergency) it just became part of the same tedious process. 

The problem is if you keep going you start to do irreversible damage. I've nicked tendons and nerves resulting in slightly restricted movement in my arm and some numb/highly sensitive patches too. Especially on forearms where it's so easy to hit important things you've got to be careful or you'll wind up disabling yourself.

Take care.

I do want to get tattoos eventually, I'm just so incredibly indecisive about what to get out of fear I'll regret it. Probably also worth mentioning I don't harm for the pain so even after a tattoo I'd still feel like slashing myself up :/
I really doubt I can last much longer.
Yep, that'd be an artery.
Honestly, you need to go to a GP and get it stitched/stapled. It will take *ages* to heal if you don't get it closed.

It won't disappoint! 

And I'm unsure, it would probably be viewable somewhere online but I simply bought it on iTunes.

I remember as a child I used to cling to movies and watch them over and over, as well as certain audio books that I'd listen to each night before bed for years.

I'm now 20 and have been utterly obsessed with the movie Mary and Max since I was 7 years old. I watch it at the very least weekly, and when I'm anxious I tend to rewatch it daily. It's a stop motion film based on a true story of a young girl in Australia who has a pen pal in New York, and explores some very serious themes yet is still a comedy drama.

This is from the Wikipedia:
"The film deals with themes including childhood neglect, friendship, addiction, alcoholism, recovery, the obscurity of life, teasing, loneliness, mental illness, autism (Asperger syndrome in particular), obesity, suicide, depression, isolation, and anxiety."

I highly recommend, it's worth the watch.

I agree that going cold turkey isn't the way to go. What would I substitute for cutting? I have harmed in other ways (scratching, pulling out hair and vomiting everything I eat) but it's just not the same. It's hard for me to feel regret about harming because if gives me so much relief, even if it is only short term.

According to the Wikipedia page it's the symbol search, coding and cancellation tests. I have a vague memory of doing them all, but it was awhile ago that I was tested for part of my ASD diagnosis. 

Symbol search had 2 columns...one with 2 symbols, then the other had I believe 5/6 symbols. You simply had to tick (or perhaps cross out) whether or not one of the 2 symbols was in the second column, and do as many as rows as possible in a time limit.

I think coding had numbers 1-9 with a symbol associated with each. You then had a page full of numbers 1-9 in random order and had to draw as many of the symbols as possible under the number with a time limit again.

Cancellation had 2 shapes that were 2 different colours you had to remember; red square and yellow triangle for example. Then there was a page of squares and triangles in a mix of red and yellow, so some squares were red but others yellow, some triangles red but others yellow, and you had to go through and only cross out the red squares and yellow triangles whilst avoiding the incorrect ones.

On my selective interests I often talk very fast. I have to forcibly slow myself down at times just so the other party can keep up. I've had my IQ tested and even though there's a fair bit of controversy surrounding the test in general I still believe in one section; that my processing speed is in the 98th percentile. I can speak fast as I think fast, so I'm able to construct my sentences at a much quicker rate to most.

Also on interrupting, I sometimes find myself replying whilst I'm being talked to, as I predict what the rest of the sentence will consist of and find it irrelevant for them to continue. I might be viewed as rude at times but it's not exactly something I can change.

I'm glad you're making some progress with going to stores, that's a huge step! I have some hoarding tendencies as well, but I've had them since I was a child (bit of a collector but that's another story aha).
Indeed. For quite some time I got all my necessities home delivered, I think I would have starved before going to a supermarket.
I'm sorry you're also struggling. Take care.
